title: Saturation/openness of N in Proj S unproven (Lemma lem:Nopen)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma `lem:Nopen` (Section \ref{sec:proj}) and its use in Step 2 of Proposition `prop:iso-onto-image`.

**Gap.** The proof asserts that the problem's target $N=\mathbb{P}Z/\!\!/G$ is *canonically an open subscheme* of $\operatorname{Proj}S=\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)/\!\!/G$, identified with $\pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathbb{P}Z\cap\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^{ss})$. This requires
$$\pi_{\mathcal W}^{-1}\big(\pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathbb{P}Z\cap\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^{ss})\big)=\mathbb{P}Z\cap\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^{ss}\quad(\text{saturation}).$$

The stated justification — "a semistable point is in $\mathbb{P}Z$ iff its unique closed orbit in its semistable closure is, because $\mathbb{P}Z$ is open and $G$-invariant" — is a **non-sequitur and is false in general**. For a *strictly semistable* $w\in\mathbb{P}Z\cap ss$, the fiber $\pi_{\mathcal W}^{-1}(\pi_{\mathcal W}(w))$ contains every semistable point whose orbit closure meets the unique closed orbit $C\subset\overline{Gw}$. An open invariant set may contain $w$ while $C\not\subset\mathbb{P}Z$: the regular-sequence condition is open but typically **not saturated**, since a closed-orbit degeneration of a regular sequence need not remain a regular sequence. Then the set is not saturated, $\pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathbb{P}Z\cap ss)$ need not be open, and the good quotient of $\mathbb{P}Z$ (the problem's $N$) need not embed as an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Proj}S$ (the map may fail injectivity or openness).

**Consequence.** Without the open immersion $j:N\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}S$, the identification $j\circ\mathbb{P}\nabla=\iota|_M$ used to deduce that $\mathbb{P}\nabla$ is a locally closed immersion collapses, and "$Y$ is a *normal subvariety of $N$*" is not established.

**What must be proved.** Either (a) that $\mathbb{P}Z\cap\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^{ss}$ is saturated; or, more robustly, (b) that $\nabla(\mathbb{P}X)$ lies in the **stable** locus $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^s$ (see companion issue), where quotients are geometric and every invariant open is automatically saturated within the stable locus, so the identification of $N$ becomes legitimate on the relevant region.
